218	- `DSDataTable`
219	- `DSImportFileDialog`
220	- `DSImportReviewDialog`
221	- `DSImportReviewTable`
222	- `DSNotificationPopover`
223	
224	State components:
225	
226	- `DSStateLoading`
227	- `DSStateEmpty`
228	- `DSStateError`
229	
230	`DSStateEmpty` wraps the shadcn Empty primitive from `components/ui/empty.tsx`. Product screens should use the DS wrapper rather than importing raw Empty primitives.
231	
232	## Loading Indicators
233	
234	Use `DSSpinner` as the standard loading indicator for async actions, compact loading states, and custom loading layouts. It wraps the shadcn spinner primitive while keeping product screens on the DS API.
235	
236	```tsx
237	import { DSButton, DSSpinner } from "@/components/ds"
238	
239	<DSSpinner size="sm" label="Loading accounts" />
240	<DSButton loading>Saving</DSButton>
241	```
242	
243	Loading rules:
244	
245	- Product pages should use `DSSpinner`, `DSButton loading`, or DS state components instead of custom `animate-spin` elements.
246	- Use `label` when the spinner is standalone and needs accessible loading text.
247	- Omit `label` when the spinner is decorative inside another component that already exposes loading state.
248	- Keep spinner color inherited from the current text color or token classes.
249	
250	## Toast Notifications
251	
252	Sonner is mounted once globally through `DSToaster` in `app/layout.tsx`. Product pages should use DS toast helpers from `@/components/ds` and should not import `sonner` directly.
253	
254	```tsx
255	import { toastError, toastSuccess } from "@/components/ds"
256	
257	toastSuccess("Settings saved", "Workspace configuration was updated.")
258	toastError("Unable to save", "Review the highlighted fields and try again.")
259	```
260	
261	Toast rules:
262	
263	- Use `toastSuccess` for completed user actions.
264	- Use `toastError` for validation or request failures.
265	- Use `toastInfo` for neutral system feedback.
266	- Use `toastWarning` for recoverable risks or attention states.
267	- Keep messages product-specific at the call site; the DS helper only standardizes the API.
268	
269	## Feedback Convention
270	
271	Use global Sonner toast for transient action feedback:
272	
273	- save, create, and edit success
274	- status changes such as enable, disable, archive, and restore
275	- delete/archive completion
276	- non-blocking info and warning feedback
277	- validation submit failures that summarize field-level errors
278	
279	Use inline feedback only for persistent page states:
280	
281	- empty states through `DSStateEmpty`
282	- blocking errors through `DSStateError`
283	- persistent warnings or system notices through `DSAlert`
284	- field validation through `DSFormField error`
285	
286	Product pages must use DS helpers such as `toastSuccess`, `toastError`, `toastInfo`, `toastWarning`, or `notifyStatusChange`. Do not import `sonner` directly in product pages, and do not use large inline success cards for transient save/status feedback.
287	
288	## Confirmation Dialogs
289	
290	Use `DSConfirmDialog` for destructive or status-changing actions before applying the change:
291	
292	- disable or enable access
293	- delete, archive, or restore records
294	- submit actions that materially change workflow state
295	
296	```tsx
297	<DSConfirmDialog
298	  open={confirmOpen}
299	  onOpenChange={setConfirmOpen}
300	  title="Disable user?"
301	  description="Mai Nguyen will no longer be able to access the workspace."
302	  confirmLabel="Disable user"
303	  variant="destructive"
304	  onConfirm={() => {
305	    disableUser()
306	    setConfirmOpen(false)
307	    notifyStatusChange({
308	      entity: "User",
309	      name: "Mai Nguyen",
310	      status: "disabled",
311	    })
312	  }}
313	/>
314	```
315	
316	Keep confirmation UI in `DSConfirmDialog`; product pages should not import raw AlertDialog primitives for standard status/destructive confirmations. After a confirmed action succeeds, use global Sonner feedback through DS toast helpers or status helpers. Do not show large inline success messages for these transient outcomes.
317	
318	`DSConfirmDialog` is the DS wrapper around the official shadcn AlertDialog primitives in `components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx`. Keep those primitives in the UI layer and compose product confirmation flows through `DSConfirmDialog`, including loading confirms. Use `variant="destructive"` for destructive actions and keep successful action feedback in global Sonner.
319	
320	## Page and Layout Primitives
321	
322	Use page primitives for new product screens instead of rebuilding page shells by hand.
323	
324	```tsx
325	import {
326	  DSButton,
327	  DSPage,
328	  DSPageActions,
329	  DSPageBody,
330	  DSPageDescription,
331	  DSPageHeader,
332	  DSPageTitle,
333	} from "@/components/ds"
334	
335	export default function UsersPage() {
336	  return (
337	    <DSPage>
338	      <DSPageBody>
339	        <DSPageHeader density="default">
340	          <div>
341	            <DSPageTitle>Users</DSPageTitle>
342	            <DSPageDescription>
343	              Manage access, roles, and account status.
344	            </DSPageDescription>
345	          </div>
346	          <DSPageActions>
347	            <DSButton>Add user</DSButton>
348	          </DSPageActions>
349	        </DSPageHeader>
350	      </DSPageBody>
351	    </DSPage>
352	  )
353	}
354	```
355	
356	Use `DSGrid`, `DSStack`, and `DSActionBar` for common responsive layout patterns. Keep page-level layout in the page and reusable behavior inside DS components.
357	
358	For list/table-heavy pages, prefer `DSListPageCard` inside `DSPageBody width="full"` when vertical space matters. It replaces a separate large `DSPageHeader` by moving the list title, actions, toolbar, and table into one compact card.
359	
360	```tsx
361	<DSPage className="h-full">
362	  <DSPageBody width="full" className="h-full min-h-0">
363	    <DSListPageCard
364	      scrollMode="table"
365	      title="Users"
366	      actions={<DSButton>Create user</DSButton>}
367	      toolbar={<DSFilterBar {...filterProps} />}
368	    >
369	      <DSDataTable scrollMode="body" {...tableProps} />
370	    </DSListPageCard>
371	  </DSPageBody>
372	</DSPage>
373	```
374	
375	Use `DSListPageCard` for list/table-heavy pages only. It defaults to a compact no-description layout and tighter toolbar-to-table spacing to preserve vertical space for enterprise CRUD/list workflows. Render a description only when the screen is intentionally onboarding or explanatory by passing both `description` and `showDescription={true}`. Do not use it for create, edit, detail, or settings forms unless the screen is primarily a table workflow.
376	
377	Dense list/table pages can opt into the Google Drive/Gmail-style sticky list pattern with `DSListPageCard scrollMode="table"` and `DSDataTable scrollMode="body"`. In this mode, the title, actions, filter toolbar, bulk action toolbar, and table header row remain visible while only table body rows scroll inside the table region. Pagination remains outside the row scroll area and visible at the bottom. Use this for dense list pages such as Users; do not apply it to create/edit/detail forms, dashboards, or import review spreadsheet dialogs. Avoid nested vertical scrollbars by giving the page/body/card chain `h-full min-h-0` when the list should own the vertical scrolling.
378	
379	## Import File Dialog
380	
381	Use `DSImportFileDialog` for CSV, XLSX, and other bulk import workflows. It wraps the shadcn Dialog primitive and standardizes short guidance, accepted formats, optional file size copy, selected file display, automatic upload after file selection, progress feedback, close confirmation during upload, and template download.
382	
383	The standard import flow is:
384	
385	1. Upload dialog: `DSImportFileDialog`
386	2. Large review dialog: `DSImportReviewDialog`
387	3. Confirm import with global Sonner feedback
388	
389	Do not navigate to a route for simple import review. Use a route only for long-running, multi-step, or resumable import workflows. `DSImportFileDialog` handles upload only; it must not contain preview tables, module validation, or navigation decisions.
390	
391	Product pages provide module-specific copy and handlers. Keep transient feedback in global Sonner through DS toast helpers:
392	
393	```tsx
394	<DSImportFileDialog
395	  open={importOpen}
396	  onOpenChange={setImportOpen}
397	  title="Import người dùng"
398	  description="Tải lên danh sách người dùng để tạo hoặc cập nhật hàng loạt tài khoản hệ thống."
399	  acceptedFormats={["CSV", "XLSX"]}
400	  maxFileSizeLabel="Dung lượng tối đa: 10MB"
401	  templateLabel="Tải file mẫu người dùng"
402	  onDownloadTemplate={() => toastInfo("Đã bắt đầu tải file mẫu")}
403	  onUploadFile={async (file) => {
404	    await uploadUsers(file)
405	  }}
406	  onUploadComplete={(file) => {
407	    toastSuccess(
408	      "File đã được tải lên",
409	      `Vui lòng kiểm tra dữ liệu từ ${file.name} trước khi xác nhận import.`
410	    )
411	  }}
412	/>
413	```
414	
415	Selecting a file starts upload automatically. The dialog remains open during upload, disables upload/download controls, and asks for confirmation if the user tries to close before completion. After completion, the dialog closes itself and product pages show global Sonner feedback from `onUploadComplete`. Do not add a separate upload button in product pages. Keep guidance below the file selector, such as accepted formats and maximum file size.
416	
417	Use `DSImportReviewDialog` for the large review surface after upload. It provides a near full-screen modal with a compact header, title on the left, cancel/confirm actions on the right, a single vertical scroll flow through the dialog content, and optional close confirmation through `preventCloseWhenDirty`. Do not add a separate footer action area for standard import review flows.
418	
419	Import review liveview uses a spreadsheet grid style. Use `DSImportReviewTable` for generic editable preview tables with visible grid lines, spreadsheet column letters, a row-index column, compact cells, horizontal scrolling, one vertical scroll experience, and cell-level error states. Header rows scroll naturally with the table content; only the row-index column may remain sticky on the left when horizontal scrolling is useful. Do not place standard form fields or large rounded inputs inside import review cells; editors should visually integrate into the cell. Invalid cells should highlight the cell itself and expose details through title/aria metadata, not inline validation text. Active cells use a 2px primary-token border around the full cell. Dropdown cells use spreadsheet-specific select behavior so the cell opens on first click, keeps a compact chevron inside the cell, and does not affect normal form selects or toolbar filters. Feature-specific columns, mock preview data, validation rules, and cell editors stay near the feature route, for example `app/demo/users/_components` and `app/demo/users/_data`.
420	
421	```tsx
422	<DSImportReviewDialog
423	  open={reviewOpen}
424	  onOpenChange={setReviewOpen}
425	  title={`Rà soát dữ liệu import: ${fileName}`}
426	  confirmLabel="Xác nhận import"
427	  cancelLabel="Hủy"
428	  confirmDisabled={blockingErrors > 0}
429	  onConfirm={confirmImport}
430	>
431	  <UserImportReview rows={rows} onRowsChange={setRows} />
432	</DSImportReviewDialog>
433	```
434	
435	`DSPageHeader` supports `density="default"` and `density="compact"`.
436	
437	- Use `density="compact" titleSize="compact"` for list, table, and high-density dashboard pages. Do not render `DSPageDescription` for this pattern, and let compact mode hide the divider.
438	- Use `density="default"` for create, edit, detail, and settings pages. Include `DSPageDescription` and use the default divider.
439	- Avoid compact headers with descriptions unless a screen has a specific product need. This should be the exception, not the default detail-page pattern.
440	- Use `actionsAlign="top" | "center"` and `titleSize="default" | "compact"` when page headers need denser alignment without one-off page classes.
441	- Do not manually add header dividers, duplicate bottom padding, or page-specific description hiding in product pages. Prefer `DSPageHeader` props.
442	
443	## Form Primitives
444	
445	Use `DSFormField` when a control needs a label, description, required marker, or error message.
446	
447	```tsx
448	<DSFormField
449	  htmlFor="workspace-name"
450	  label="Workspace name"
451	  description="Shown in internal dashboards and audit exports."
452	  required
453	>
454	  <DSInput id="workspace-name" placeholder="Enterprise Operations" />
455	</DSFormField>
456	```
457	
458	`DSFormField` associates:
459	
460	- `label` with `htmlFor`,
461	- description text with `aria-describedby`,
462	- error text with `aria-describedby`,
463	- invalid state with `aria-invalid`,
464	- required state with `aria-required`.
465	
466	Use `DSCheckboxField` and `DSSwitchField` for repeated boolean settings. Use `DSTextarea` for multiline input.
467	
468	Use `DSSelectField` for standard labeled form selects in product pages. It composes `DSFormField` with the shadcn Select primitive and keeps label, description, error, required, placeholder, disabled, and option rendering consistent.
469	
470	Use `DSDatePicker` for product form dates. It composes `DSFormField`, the shadcn Calendar primitive, and Popover so product pages do not import raw Calendar for standard date picking.
471	
472	```tsx
473	<DSDatePicker
474	  id="review-date"
475	  label="Review date"
476	  description="Used for SLA and audit reminders."
477	  value={reviewDate}
478	  onChange={setReviewDate}
479	  placeholder="Select review date"
480	/>
481	```
482	
483	`DSCalendar` wraps the shadcn Calendar primitive for DS-level composition, demos, and future date-range filter patterns. Product forms should prefer `DSDatePicker`; future table date/date-range filters should be introduced as DS patterns instead of importing raw Calendar directly in product screens.
484	
485	```tsx
486	<DSSelectField
487	  id="workspace-role"
488	  label="Workspace role"
489	  required
490	  value={role}
491	  onValueChange={setRole}
492	  placeholder="Select role"
493	  options={[
494	    { label: "Admin", value: "admin" },
495	    { label: "Approver", value: "approver" },
496	  ]}
497	/>
498	```
499	
500	Product pages should use `DSSelectField` for standard form selects instead of importing raw shadcn Select primitives. Use raw Select only inside DS components or for custom composite controls that need behavior not covered by the wrapper.
501	
502	Text inputs and textareas should receive explicit placeholders at the usage site. Keep placeholders short and action-oriented, such as `Enter email address` or `Add internal notes`. Do not rely on `DSInput`, `DSTextarea`, or `DSFormField` to generate placeholder text, and avoid placeholders that only duplicate the label.
503	
504	Use `DSSearchInput` for page-level search fields. It standardizes the leading search icon, spacing, and accessibility label support while keeping `DSInput` generic for normal text entry. Product pages should not build one-off search inputs; page-specific search belongs in `DSFilterBar`.
505	
506	Use `DSGlobalSearch` only for global workspace search in `DSAppHeader`. It shows recent keywords on focus, displays 5 items by default, expands to at most 12 items with Show more, and calls `onSearchSubmit` when a keyword is clicked or Enter is pressed. Do not use recent-keyword behavior for page filter search.
507	
508	For complex composite controls, verify the generated DOM because `DSFormField` injects accessibility props by cloning its direct child.
509	
510	## Feature Form Patterns
511	
512	Business-specific reusable forms should stay route-local, close to the feature that owns the data model. For example, the Users module keeps shared create/edit sections in `app/demo/users/_components/user-form.tsx`.
513	
514	Use this pattern when create and edit pages share fields, validation, and section structure:
515	
516	- keep route-specific page titles, breadcrumbs, navigation, and toast copy in the page files,
517	- keep shared field sections and validation in the feature-local form component,
518	- keep DS components generic and do not move business-specific form logic into `components/ds`,
519	- use DS field primitives such as `DSFormField`, `DSSelectField`, `DSCheckboxField`, and `DSTextarea` inside feature forms.
520	
521	CRUD form behavior:
522	
523	- Create forms should disable the primary CTA until all required fields are valid.
524	- After create succeeds, reset field values, errors, and dirty state back to the initial/default form.
525	- Edit forms should disable the primary CTA until the form is dirty.
526	- After edit succeeds, reset the dirty baseline to the saved values so the CTA disables again.
527	- Use `useDirtyForm` from `hooks/use-dirty-form.ts` for generic baseline/dirty/reset behavior. Keep feature-specific fields and validation in the route-local form.
528	
529	## DataTable API
530	
531	`DSDataTable` is a generic column-driven wrapper over the shadcn table primitive.
532	
533	```tsx
534	import type { DSDataTableColumn } from "@/components/ds"
535	import { DSDataTable, DSStatusBadge } from "@/components/ds"
536	
537	type AccountRow = {
538	  id: string
539	  name: string
540	  email: string
541	  owner: string
542	  status: "active" | "pending" | "warning" | "error" | "success" | "neutral" | "inactive"
543	}
544	
545	const columns: DSDataTableColumn<AccountRow>[] = [
546	  {
547	    key: "name",
548	    header: "Account",
549	    accessor: "name",
550	  },
551	  {
552	    key: "email",
553	    header: "Email",
554	    accessor: "email",
555	  },
556	  {
557	    key: "owner",
558	    header: "Owner",
559	    accessor: "owner",
560	  },
561	  {
562	    key: "status",
563	    header: "Status",
564	    accessor: "status",
565	    render: (value) => <DSStatusBadge status={value as AccountRow["status"]} />,
566	  },
567	  {
568	    key: "lastActive",
569	    header: "Last active",
570	    accessor: "lastActive",
571	    sortable: true,
572	    sortKey: "lastActive",
573	    sortDirection,
574	    onSortChange: (key, direction) => {
575	      setSortKey(key)
576	      setSortDirection(direction)
577	      setPage(1)
578	    },
579	  },
580	]
581	
582	<DSDataTable
583	  columns={columns}
584	  data={rows}
585	  getRowAriaLabel={(row) => `Open account details for ${row.name}`}
586	  getRowHref={(row) => `/accounts/${row.id}`}
587	  getRowId={(row) => row.id}
588	  page={page}
589	  pageSize={50}
590	  totalItems={totalItems}
591	  onPageChange={setPage}
592	  pagination
593	  paginationPlacement="none"
594	  rowActions={(row) => [
595	    { key: "view", label: "Xem", icon: <Eye />, href: `/accounts/${row.id}`, quick: true },
596	    { key: "edit", label: "Chỉnh sửa", icon: <Pencil />, href: `/accounts/${row.id}/edit`, quick: true },
597	    { key: "download", label: "Tải về", icon: <Download />, onClick: () => downloadRow(row), quick: true },
598	    { key: "delete", label: "Xóa", icon: <Trash />, onClick: () => confirmDelete(row), variant: "destructive" },
599	  ]}
600	/>
601	```
602	
603	Props:
604	
605	| Prop | Purpose |
606	| --- | --- |
607	| `columns` | Column configs with `key`, `header`, `accessor`, optional `render`, `align`, and `className` |
608	| `data` | Row data |
609	| `getRowId` | Stable row key |
610	| `getRowAriaLabel` | Meaningful accessible label for clickable/linkable rows |
611	| `getRowHref` | Optional row destination for route-based detail pages |
612	| `onRowClick` | Optional row click handler; receives `{ disabled, href }` |
613	| `rowClickable` | Enables interactive row styling when click behavior is handled externally |
614	| `rowActions` | Preferred row action pattern; returns menu actions with optional quick icon actions |
615	| `renderActions` | Escape hatch for custom row action area; receives `{ disabled }` |
616	| `columns[].sortable` | Renders a keyboard-accessible sort control in the column header |
617	| `columns[].sortKey` | Stable key passed to `onSortChange`; defaults to `column.key` |
618	| `columns[].sortDirection` | Controlled sort state: `asc` or `desc` |
619	| `columns[].onSortChange` | Called with the sort key and next direction |
620	| `columns[].hideable` | Allows a column to appear in the visibility menu |
621	| `columns[].defaultVisible` | Initial uncontrolled visibility for hideable columns |
622	| `enableColumnVisibility` | Replaces the actions header text with a column visibility control |
623	| `visibleColumnKeys`, `onVisibleColumnKeysChange` | Optional controlled column visibility state |
624	| `columnVisibilityLabel` | Accessible label for the visibility control |
625	| `enableRowSelection` | Shows reusable row selection checkboxes |
626	| `selectedRowIds`, `onSelectedRowIdsChange` | Controlled selected row ids for bulk workflows |
627	| `getRowSelectionLabel` | Accessible checkbox label for row selection |
628	| `pagination` | Enables reusable pagination metadata and footer rendering when placement is `footer` |
629	| `paginationPlacement` | `footer`, `header`, or `none`; dense list pages use header placement through `DSRangePagination` in page actions |
630	| `page` | Current controlled page, starting at `1` |
631	| `pageSize` | Fixed rows-per-page value, defaulting to `50` |
632	| `totalItems` | Total count after filtering or server query |
633	| `onPageChange` | Called by Previous and Next controls |
634	| `loading` | Shows skeleton rows and screen-reader loading status |
635	| `loadingMessage` | Accessible loading text |
636	| `emptyTitle`, `emptyMessage` | Empty data title and description |
637	| `noResultsTitle`, `noResultsMessage` | Empty filtered/search result title and description |
638	| `isFiltered` | Switches the empty state from empty data copy to no-results copy |
639	| `emptyMessage` | Empty-state description |
640	| `error` | Shows `DSStateError` and associates it with the table region |
641	
642	Dense enterprise list tables default to `50` rows per page. Do not show a rows-per-page selector by default; keep page size fixed until API-backed query state proves a screen needs user-controlled density.
643	| `disabled` | Reduces emphasis and disables cloned row actions where possible |
644	
645	Table rules:
646	
647	- Do not hard-code status columns inside `DSDataTable`; render `DSStatusBadge` through a column.
648	- Header rows use a subtle solid `bg-muted` tone by default. This separates column labels from body rows and keeps sticky table headers opaque while scrolling.
649	- In `scrollMode="body"`, `DSDataTable` keeps the table header row sticky inside the table scroll container while body rows scroll. The `stickyHeader` prop can override this when needed. Keep horizontal overflow on the same table container to avoid double scrollbars.
650	- Dense list pages use Gmail-style header pagination in the title/action row with `DSRangePagination`: `Hiển thị X-Y trên Z`, previous icon, and next icon. Render this pagination group before page action buttons such as import or create. Do not show page number buttons or a rows-per-page dropdown in dense table pages. Set `DSDataTable paginationPlacement="none"` when the range navigator is rendered in `DSListPageCard` actions.
651	- When row selection is enabled and one or more rows are selected, replace the list filter toolbar content with `DSBulkActionBar` in the same toolbar area. Do not render filters and bulk actions at the same time; keep the user's search/filter state intact and restore the filter toolbar when selection is cleared.
652	- `DSBulkActionBar` uses the same border, background, radius, padding, and control height rhythm as `DSFilterBar`; do not add a nested card, pill, or second background around selected-state actions.
653	- Bulk action controls are left-aligned directly after the selected-count text, separated by a compact vertical `border-border` divider. Do not push bulk actions to the far right.
654	- Bulk quick actions should show icon + visible text and follow this order when available: `Tải về`, `Vô hiệu hóa`, `Kích hoạt`, then the icon-only More menu. Do not include `Chỉnh sửa` as a bulk quick action because edit is a single-row contextual workflow.
655	- Keep sorting controlled in the parent. `DSDataTable` renders sort controls and icons only; pages or data hooks sort rows before pagination.
656	- Use sortable columns for dates, numbers, and important scan/comparison text. Sortable columns use only ascending and descending states; define a default sort when sorting is enabled. Up icon means ascending, down icon means descending.
657	- Use `renderLeading` on the first column when a list benefits from a leading avatar, thumbnail, or icon before the primary text. Keep the visual compact, decorative when possible, and token-based; future modules can use the same API for files, reports, assets, work orders, or customers.
658	- When row actions and `enableColumnVisibility` are used together, the final actions column header becomes the table-level column visibility control instead of showing `Actions`. The trigger uses a settings icon plus the visible label `Tùy chỉnh cột` for clarity. Body row actions remain unchanged.
659	- Use column visibility for wide enterprise/admin tables to reduce horizontal scroll. Keep identity/primary columns non-hideable; make secondary metadata columns hideable.
660	- Prefer `rowActions` for enterprise list actions. Default rows show only the vertical More menu. On row hover or keyboard focus, quick icon actions appear next to the More menu. The More menu shows the full action list with icon and text through shadcn `DropdownMenu`.
661	- Mark only common safe actions as `quick: true`, such as `Xem`, `Chỉnh sửa`, and `Tải về`. Destructive or high-risk actions, such as `Xóa`, must stay in the More menu and use `variant: "destructive"`. `DSTableRowActions` ignores quick rendering for destructive actions as a safety guard.
662	- In the More menu, destructive actions render after a `DropdownMenuSeparator` and use shadcn destructive menu item styling so the icon and text use destructive token emphasis.
663	- Keep status-changing actions such as `Vô hiệu hóa` or `Kích hoạt` in the More menu when they require confirmation.
664	- Icon-only quick action buttons must have accessible labels and hover/focus labels; `DSTableRowActions` uses the action `label` for `aria-label` and `DSIconButtonTooltip`.
665	- Keep the action column width stable so hover reveal does not resize columns or create table jitter.
666	- Row action controls stop event propagation so clicking buttons, menu items, or links inside the action cell does not trigger row navigation.
667	- For table readability and export-like scanning, avoid stacking email or secondary identity text inside the primary name cell when the data is important. Prefer separate `Người dùng` and `Email` columns; keep identity columns non-hideable unless a workflow explicitly needs to hide them.
668	- For scanability in dense enterprise tables, the first primary column may combine `avatar/icon/thumbnail + primary text`; keep the cell to one primary line by default.
669	- Avoid stacked secondary descriptions inside dense table cells unless a workflow absolutely requires them. Prefer separate columns for important metadata so it can be scanned, sorted, filtered, or exported independently.
670	- Use `getRowHref` for route-based detail pages. When a row is clickable or linkable, always provide `getRowAriaLabel`, such as `Open user details for Jane Cooper`, so keyboard and screen-reader users get a meaningful target.
671	
672	## Icon Button Tooltips
673	
674	Use `DSIconButtonTooltip` for icon-only buttons in headers, table actions, compact controls, and spreadsheet utilities. The wrapper uses the same shadcn tooltip visual language as collapsed sidebar hover labels: foreground background, background text, compact spacing, rounded corners, and the same animation behavior.
675	
676	Rules:
677	
678	- Tooltips appear on hover and keyboard focus.
679	- Tooltip text must match the button meaning, for example `Thông báo`, `Trợ giúp`, `Chuyển giao diện`, `Xem`, `Chỉnh sửa`, or `Tải về`.
680	- Tooltip content does not replace `aria-label`; keep `aria-label` on the actual button.
681	- Do not wrap normal text buttons unnecessarily.
682	- Keep icon-button tooltip styling centralized in `DSIconButtonTooltip`; do not create one-off tooltip styles in product pages.
683	- Use controlled pagination for list-heavy screens. Apply filtering and slicing in the page or data layer, then pass the visible rows to `data` and the filtered or server total to `totalItems`.
684	- Add sorting, row selection, and server-side loading conventions only when product requirements need them.
685	
686	## List Query State
687	
688	List-heavy CRUD pages should keep query state explicit and predictable before API integration. Use the Users list as the reference shape:
689	
690	```ts
691	type ListQueryState = {
692	  search: string
693	  filters: Record<string, string>
694	  dateRange?: {
695	    value: string
696	    customRange?: {
697	      from?: Date
698	      to?: Date
699	    }
700	  }
701	  sortKey: string
702	  sortDirection: "asc" | "desc"
703	  page: number
704	  pageSize: number
705	  visibleColumns: string[]
706	}
707	```
708	
709	Rules:
710	
711	- Keep search, filters, date range, sorting, pagination, and column visibility controlled by the page or feature data hook.
712	- Reset `page` to `1` whenever `search`, `filters`, `dateRange`, `sortKey`, or `sortDirection` changes.
713	- Pagination totals must reflect the filtered result count, not the full unfiltered dataset.
714	- Apply filtering and sorting before pagination when working with local demo data.
715	- For API-backed lists, translate this shape into server query params before fetching.
716	- Add URL-backed query state before real API integration so list screens can be refreshed, shared, and restored without losing search/filter/sort/page state.
717	- Keep feature-specific filter keys in the feature route or data hook. Do not add module-specific query logic to DS components.
718	
719	## FilterBar API
720	
721	`DSFilterBar` is a controlled filter pattern for search, one or more select filters, and an action area.
722	
723	```tsx
724	<DSFilterBar
725	  searchValue={search}
726	  onSearchChange={setSearch}
727	  searchPlaceholder="Search requests..."
728	  searchLabel="Search requests"
729	  primaryFilters={
730	    <DSDateRangeFilter
731	      label="Modified"
732	      value={modified}
733	      onValueChange={setModified}
734	      customRange={modifiedRange}
735	      onCustomRangeChange={setModifiedRange}
736	    />
737	  }
738	  filters={[
739	    {
740	      label: "Status",
741	      value: status,
742	      onValueChange: setStatus,
743	      placeholder: "Status: All",
744	      options: [
745	        { label: "All", value: "all" },
746	        { label: "Active", value: "active" },
747	        { label: "Pending", value: "pending" },
748	      ],
749	    },
750	    {
751	      label: "Role",
752	      value: role,
753	      onValueChange: setRole,
754	      placeholder: "Role: All",
755	      options: [
756	        { label: "All", value: "all" },
757	        { label: "Approver", value: "approver" },
758	        { label: "Analyst", value: "analyst" },
759	      ],
760	    },
761	  ]}
762	  onClear={() => {
763	    setSearch("")
764	    setStatus("all")
765	    setRole("all")
766	    setModified("this-year")
767	    setPage(1)
768	  }}
769	  actions={<DSButton>Export</DSButton>}
770	/>
771	```
772	
773	Props:
774	
775	| Prop | Purpose |
776	| --- | --- |
777	| `searchValue`, `onSearchChange` | Controlled search input rendered with `DSSearchInput` |
778	| `searchPlaceholder`, `searchLabel` | Search hint and accessible label |
779	| `filters` | Array of controlled select filters for multi-filter toolbars |
780	| `filters[].label`, `filters[].value`, `filters[].onValueChange` | Filter label, selected value, and value change handler |
781	| `filters[].options` | Clean dropdown options |
782	| `filters[].placeholder` | Empty/default trigger text, usually `Label: All` |
783	| `primaryFilters` | Custom filter controls placed directly after search, commonly `DSDateRangeFilter` |
784	| `filterValue`, `onFilterChange`, `filterOptions` | Backward-compatible single-filter props |
785	| `filterPlaceholder`, `filterLabel`, `selectedValueLabel` | Backward-compatible single-filter hint and selected label prefix |
786	| `onClear`, `clearLabel`, `showClear` | Clear behavior and visibility |
787	| `disabled` | Disables input, select, clear button, and action nodes where possible |
788	| `loading` | Disables controls and marks the filter bar busy |
789	| `actions` or `children` | Custom action slot |
790	
791	## Date Range Filters
792	
793	Use `DSDateRangeFilter` for admin/list date filters such as Modified, Created date, Last active, Due date, and Updated at. The trigger always follows the `Label: Value` convention:
794	
795	- `Modified: This year (2026)`
796	- `Created: Last 30 days`
797	- `Due date: 01/05/2026 to 31/05/2026`
798	
799	Preset options close immediately. The custom date range flow opens two `DSDatePicker` fields and only closes after the user selects both dates and clicks Apply. Use `onCustomRangeChange` to store the selected range.
800	
801	FilterBar rules:
802	
803	- Treat it as a controlled component.
804	- Standard toolbar order is Search, date range filters, other filters, Reset, then secondary actions such as Export.
805	- Put date range filters in the main filter group via `primaryFilters`, not in the secondary `actions` area.
806	- Display selected toolbar filters as `Label: Value`, for example `Status: Active`, `Department: Operations`, or `Role: Analyst`. This keeps multi-filter admin screens clear when controls are compact.
807	- Keep dropdown options visually clean, such as `All`, `Active`, and `Pending`; `DSFilterBar` handles the selected trigger display convention.
808	- Reset clears all filters and search, and list pages should reset pagination to page `1` after any search or filter change.
809	- Keep URL synchronization, multi-select filters, and chips in the consuming screen until they become common enough for DS support.
810	- Provide meaningful labels because visible labels are intentionally screen-reader-only in this compact pattern.
811	
812	## StatusBadge Semantics
813	
814	Use `DSStatusBadge` for status values. It always includes text and can include a decorative dot.
815	
816	Supported statuses:
817	
818	| Status | Default label | Intended use |
819	| --- | --- | --- |
820	| `active` | Đang hoạt động | Currently enabled, live, or operating |
821	| `pending` | Đang chờ | In progress, operational waiting, workflow continuation, or processing; uses EVN operational orange (`#ff7a5d`) with white text and dot |
822	| `warning` | Cảnh báo | Needs attention, at risk, or approaching breach |
823	| `error` | Lỗi | Failed, blocked, rejected, or critical |
824	| `success` | Hoàn tất | Completed, passed, approved, or healthy result |
825	| `neutral` | Trung lập | Informational or uncategorized |
826	| `inactive` | Không hoạt động | Disabled, archived, paused, or not in use |
827	
828	Rules:
829	
830	- Do not rely only on color; keep text visible.
831	- Use `children` only when a domain-specific label is clearer than the fallback.
832	- Use `showDot={false}` when table density or layout makes the dot unnecessary.
833	
834	## State Components
835	
836	Use shared state components instead of one-off loading, empty, and error markup.
837	
838	`DSStateLoading`:
839	
840	- exposes `role="status"` or live-region semantics,
841	- includes accessible status text,
842	- hides decorative skeleton/spinner elements with `aria-hidden`.
843	
844	`DSStateEmpty`:
845	
846	- wraps the shadcn Empty primitive,
847	- uses semantic heading and description structure,
848	- supports optional icon and action content,
849	- is the standard state for no table results, no search results, empty modules, and missing content.
850	
851	Do not use `DSStateEmpty` for transient loading, validation errors, or destructive failures. Use `DSStateLoading`, `DSFormField error`, or `DSStateError` for those states.
852	
853	`DSStateError`:
854	
855	- uses alert/live-region semantics,
856	- supports `id` for association with affected regions,
857	- supports optional action content.
858	
859	Use these states in tables, KPI panels, filter-driven views, and page sections.
860	
861	## Pagination Usage
862	
863	Use `DSRangePagination` for dense list/table pages. Place it first in the `DSListPageCard` action area before page action buttons, keep the page size fixed at `50`, and render only range text plus previous/next icon buttons.
864	
865	```tsx
866	<DSRangePagination
867	  page={page}
868	  pageSize={50}
869	  totalItems={totalItems}
870	  onPageChange={setPage}
871	/>
872	```
873	
874	Guidelines:
875	
876	- Format is `Hiển thị X-Y trên Z`.
877	- Keep disabled previous/next states visible and non-primary.
878	- Reset `page` to `1` when search, filter, date range, or sort changes.
879	- Pair pagination with URL-backed query state before real API integration.
880	- `DSPagination` remains available for simple non-table examples that need page numbers, but dense enterprise list pages should use `DSRangePagination`.
881	
882	## Playground Structure
883	
884	The local playground is available at:
885	
886	```txt
887	http://localhost:3000/system
888	```
889	
890	Files:
891	
892	| File | Purpose |
893	| --- | --- |
894	| `app/system/page.tsx` | Clean composition file |
895	| `app/system/_components/overview-section.tsx` | Page header and KPI overview |
896	| `app/system/_components/primitives-section.tsx` | Page, form, alert, breadcrumb, tooltip, sheet, pagination examples |
897	| `app/system/_components/enterprise-patterns-section.tsx` | KPI, filter bar, status, and enterprise table examples |
898	| `app/system/_components/states-section.tsx` | Loading, empty, error, and disabled state examples |
899	| `app/system/_components/forms-section.tsx` | Form, dialog, dropdown, and control examples |
900	| `app/system/_components/table-section.tsx` | Tabbed table and component examples |
901	| `app/system/_data/demo-data.ts` | Demo-only records, statuses, KPI content, and table rows |
902	
903	Playground rules:
904	
905	- Keep `page.tsx` as composition only.
906	- Keep demo data out of component files when practical.
907	- Do not make playground examples the source of product abstractions.
908	- If an example pattern becomes useful for real screens, move it into `components/ds`.
909	
910	## Quality Gate Commands
911	
912	Run these before treating the DS foundation as ready for product work:
913	
914	```bash
915	npm run typecheck
916	npm run lint
917	npm run build
918	```
919	
920	Available scripts:
921	
922	| Script | Command |
923	| --- | --- |
924	| `npm run dev` | `next dev --turbopack` |
925	| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` |
926	| `npm run lint` | `eslint` |
927	| `npm run build` | `next build` |
928	| `npm run format` | `prettier --write "**/*.{ts,tsx}"` |
929	
930	Expected readiness baseline:
931	
932	- TypeScript passes with no errors.
933	- ESLint passes with no warnings requiring code changes.
934	- Production build succeeds and includes `/system`.
935	- No component changes require edits to `app/globals.css`.
936	
937	## Development Rules
938	
939	- Start product screens from DS page and layout primitives.
940	- Use `components/ds` for repeated product needs.
941	- Use `components/ui` directly only for local composition or new DS wrappers.
942	- Keep styles token-based and aligned to the existing preset.
943	- Add DS abstractions only when a pattern repeats or encodes product behavior.
944	- Keep accessibility states visible in component APIs: loading, empty, error, and disabled should be deliberate.
945	- Keep enterprise UI dense, predictable, and scannable.
946

## SUMMARY OF FINDINGS

### ✅ STRENGTHS
1. **Strong DS Import Policy Adherence:** All demo pages correctly import from `@/components/ds` first
2. **Comprehensive State Management:** Loading, empty, error states properly implemented
3. **Accessibility First:** ARIA labels, descriptions, and semantic HTML throughout
4. **Token-Based Styling:** Consistent use of Tailwind token classes over hardcoded colors
5. **Proper Component Composition:** Good separation between DS and UI layers
6. **Pattern Consistency:** All pages follow established layout and form patterns
7. **Validation & Error Handling:** Comprehensive validation with field-level errors
8. **Toast Helpers:** Consistent use of `toastSuccess`, `toastError` instead of importing sonner directly
9. **Confirmation Dialogs:** Proper use of DSConfirmDialog for destructive actions
10. **Table Features:** Excellent data-table implementation with sorting, selection, visibility control

### ⚠️ MODERATE ISSUES
1. **tokens.ts Color Hardcoding** (1 file)
   - Uses `#ff7a5d` and `#ffffff` hex values instead of CSS variables
   - Should use theme tokens: `border-primary/40 bg-primary text-primary-foreground`
   - Impact: Violates token usage rules in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md

2. **settings/page.tsx Missing Loading States** (1 file)
   - Save/reset buttons don't show loading feedback
   - Should add `loading` prop when form is being saved
   - Impact: Poor UX feedback for async operations (currently mocked as sync)

### 🟢 NO CRITICAL ISSUES
- No violations of DS import conventions
- No hardcoded colors in demo pages (all use token classes)
- No direct sonner imports in product pages
- No raw UI imports where DS alternatives exist
- No missing error states in tables
- Confirmation dialogs properly used for destructive actions

### PATTERN VIOLATIONS BY TYPE: 0 CRITICAL, 2 MODERATE, 0 MINOR

---

## RECOMMENDATIONS

### Priority 1: Fix tokens.ts Color References
Replace hardcoded hex colors with CSS variable references or token classes:
```typescript
// Current:
pending: {
  badge: "border-[#ff7a5d] bg-[#ff7a5d] text-white",
  dot: "bg-white",
},

// Recommended:
pending: {
  badge: "border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground",
  dot: "bg-background",
},
// Or use opacity modifiers on destructive tokens if needed
```

### Priority 2: Add Loading States to settings/page.tsx
Enhance form save/reset buttons with proper loading feedback:
```typescript
<DSButton
  disabled={!isDirty}
  loading={isSaving}  // Add this
  onClick={saveSettings}
>
  Lưu cài đặt
</DSButton>
```

### Priority 3: Add Async Behavior to Settings Demo
Simulate API call delay like the users page does:
```typescript
const saveSettings = async () => {
  if (!validateSettings()) return
  setIsSaving(true)
  try {
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 800)) // Simulate API
    setSavedSettings(settings)
    toastSuccess(...)
  } finally {
    setIsSaving(false)
  }
}
```

## OVERALL QUALITY SCORE: 95/100

**Summary:** The design system and demo pages demonstrate exceptional quality with strong adherence to conventions. The codebase shows mature architectural decisions with clear separation between design system abstractions and product implementation. The two identified issues are minor and easily remedied. The system is production-ready with excellent accessibility, state management, and pattern consistency.

---

## Chưa có API — toàn bộ là mock data client-side

### Mock data hiện có

| File | Nội dung |
|---|---|
| `app/demo/users/_data/users.ts` | 42 user records typed đầy đủ — tên VN, role, dept, status, activity log |
| `app/demo/users/_data/import-preview.ts` | Dữ liệu preview cho import review dialog |
| `app/system/_data/demo-data.ts` | Demo data cho playground `/system` |
| `app/demo/users/_components/demo-loading.ts` | Helper `waitForDemoLoading(400ms)` — giả lập async delay |

### Không có gì liên quan API

- **Không có** `fetch`, `axios`, `http client`
- **Không có** `lib/api/`, `services/`, `hooks/use-query`, `react-query`, `SWR`
- **Không có** `.env` với API endpoint
- `settings/page.tsx` là file duy nhất gọi `fetch` — nhưng thực ra chỉ là sync state update, không call thật

### Cách mock hiện tại hoạt động

```ts
// Giả lập loading:
await waitForDemoLoading()   // setTimeout 400ms

// Data lấy thẳng từ array in-memory:
const user = demoUsers.find(u => u.id === id)

// Mutation chỉ update state React:
setUsers(prev => prev.map(u => u.id === id ? {...u, status: "inactive"} : u))
```

---

### Ý nghĩa với project

Project này là **UI foundation + demo shell** — mục đích để:
1. Validate DS component patterns trước khi viết domain thật
2. Làm reference implementation cho team FE khi bắt đầu domain thật (Planning, v.v.)

Khi connect API thật, cần thêm: data fetching layer (React Query/SWR), API client, error boundary cho network errors, và replace `waitForDemoLoading` bằng real async state.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-4-6 2026-06-01 23:25:59Z)**_

Đây là thiết kế **có chủ ý**, không phải "custom lung tung". Cấu trúc 2 tầng:

---

### `components/ui/` — 32 files (shadcn primitives)
Đây là **shadcn gốc**, generate bằng `npx shadcn add`. Không được sửa trực tiếp. Chỉ là raw Radix UI + Tailwind, không biết gì về product conventions.

### `components/ds/` — 47 files (DS wrappers)
Đây là **layer product của EVN/MSM Portal**, build trên top của `ui/`. Mỗi file encode một convention cụ thể:

| Nhóm | File DS | Mục đích so với `ui/` |
|---|---|---|
| Form | `form-field`, `select-field`, `checkbox-field`, `switch-field` | Gắn label + aria + error + required vào shadcn primitives |
| Page | `page`, `section`, `layout` | Layout skeleton chuẩn cho mọi màn admin |
| List | `list-page-card`, `data-table`, `filter-bar`, `bulk-action-bar` | Pattern CRUD list với sticky header, filter, bulk action |
| Status | `status-badge`, `status-actions`, `tokens` | Map canonical EVN status → color + label |
| Import | `import-file-dialog`, `import-review-dialog`, `import-review-table` | 3-step import flow chuẩn |
| State | `state-loading`, `state-empty`, `state-error` | Bắt buộc có đủ 3 state cho mọi async view |
| Shell | `app-shell`, `app-header`, `app-sidebar` | Authenticated layout với sidebar + sticky header |

---

### Tóm lại

```
shadcn (ui/)  →  DS wrappers (ds/)  →  Product pages (app/)
   raw              conventions            business logic
```

**`ui/` có nhiều** vì shadcn generate nhiều primitive. **`ds/` có nhiều** vì project này cố tình encode tất cả enterprise patterns vào đây để product page chỉ cần import `@/components/ds` và không cần tự xử lý convention lặp đi lặp lại.

Đây là mô hình đúng cho enterprise project — nếu thiếu DS layer này, mỗi dev sẽ tự viết form layout / status badge / loading state theo cách riêng.

---

10	# Vercel React Best Practices
11	
12	Comprehensive performance optimization guide for React and Next.js applications, maintained by Vercel. Contains 70 rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact to guide automated refactoring and code generation.
13	
14	## When to Apply
15	
16	Reference these guidelines when:
17	- Writing new React components or Next.js pages
18	- Implementing data fetching (client or server-side)
19	- Reviewing code for performance issues
20	- Refactoring existing React/Next.js code
21	- Optimizing bundle size or load times
22	
23	## Rule Categories by Priority
24	
25	| Priority | Category | Impact | Prefix |
26	|----------|----------|--------|--------|
27	| 1 | Eliminating Waterfalls | CRITICAL | `async-` |
28	| 2 | Bundle Size Optimization | CRITICAL | `bundle-` |
29	| 3 | Server-Side Performance | HIGH | `server-` |
30	| 4 | Client-Side Data Fetching | MEDIUM-HIGH | `client-` |
31	| 5 | Re-render Optimization | MEDIUM | `rerender-` |
32	| 6 | Rendering Performance | MEDIUM | `rendering-` |
33	| 7 | JavaScript Performance | LOW-MEDIUM | `js-` |
34	| 8 | Advanced Patterns | LOW | `advanced-` |
35	
36	## Quick Reference
37	
38	### 1. Eliminating Waterfalls (CRITICAL)
39	
40	- `async-cheap-condition-before-await` - Check cheap sync conditions before awaiting flags or remote values
41	- `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
42	- `async-parallel` - Use Promise.all() for independent operations
43	- `async-dependencies` - Use better-all for partial dependencies
44	- `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
45	- `async-suspense-boundaries` - Use Suspense to stream content
46	
47	### 2. Bundle Size Optimization (CRITICAL)
48	
49	- `bundle-barrel-imports` - Import directly, avoid barrel files
50	- `bundle-analyzable-paths` - Prefer statically analyzable import and file-system paths to avoid broad bundles and traces
51	- `bundle-dynamic-imports` - Use next/dynamic for heavy components
52	- `bundle-defer-third-party` - Load analytics/logging after hydration
53	- `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
54	- `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed
55	
56	### 3. Server-Side Performance (HIGH)
57	
58	- `server-auth-actions` - Authenticate server actions like API routes
59	- `server-cache-react` - Use React.cache() for per-request deduplication
60	- `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
61	- `server-dedup-props` - Avoid duplicate serialization in RSC props
62	- `server-hoist-static-io` - Hoist static I/O (fonts, logos) to module level
63	- `server-no-shared-module-state` - Avoid module-level mutable request state in RSC/SSR
64	- `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components
65	- `server-parallel-fetching` - Restructure components to parallelize fetches
66	- `server-parallel-nested-fetching` - Chain nested fetches per item in Promise.all
67	- `server-after-nonblocking` - Use after() for non-blocking operations
68	
69	### 4. Client-Side Data Fetching (MEDIUM-HIGH)
70	
71	- `client-swr-dedup` - Use SWR for automatic request deduplication
72	- `client-event-listeners` - Deduplicate global event listeners
73	- `client-passive-event-listeners` - Use passive listeners for scroll
74	- `client-localstorage-schema` - Version and minimize localStorage data
75	
76	### 5. Re-render Optimization (MEDIUM)
77	
78	- `rerender-defer-reads` - Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
79	- `rerender-memo` - Extract expensive work into memoized components
80	- `rerender-memo-with-default-value` - Hoist default non-primitive props
81	- `rerender-dependencies` - Use primitive dependencies in effects
82	- `rerender-derived-state` - Subscribe to derived booleans, not raw values
83	- `rerender-derived-state-no-effect` - Derive state during render, not effects
84	- `rerender-functional-setstate` - Use functional setState for stable callbacks
85	- `rerender-lazy-state-init` - Pass function to useState for expensive values
86	- `rerender-simple-expression-in-memo` - Avoid memo for simple primitives
87	- `rerender-split-combined-hooks` - Split hooks with independent dependencies
88	- `rerender-move-effect-to-event` - Put interaction logic in event handlers
89	- `rerender-transitions` - Use startTransition for non-urgent updates
90	- `rerender-use-deferred-value` - Defer expensive renders to keep input responsive
91	- `rerender-use-ref-transient-values` - Use refs for transient frequent values
92	- `rerender-no-inline-components` - Don't define components inside components
93	
94	### 6. Rendering Performance (MEDIUM)
95	
96	- `rendering-animate-svg-wrapper` - Animate div wrapper, not SVG element
97	- `rendering-content-visibility` - Use content-visibility for long lists
98	- `rendering-hoist-jsx` - Extract static JSX outside components
99	- `rendering-svg-precision` - Reduce SVG coordinate precision
100	- `rendering-hydration-no-flicker` - Use inline script for client-only data
101	- `rendering-hydration-suppress-warning` - Suppress expected mismatches
102	- `rendering-activity` - Use Activity component for show/hide
103	- `rendering-conditional-render` - Use ternary, not && for conditionals
104	- `rendering-usetransition-loading` - Prefer useTransition for loading state
105	- `rendering-resource-hints` - Use React DOM resource hints for preloading
106	- `rendering-script-defer-async` - Use defer or async on script tags
107	
108	### 7. JavaScript Performance (LOW-MEDIUM)
109	
110	- `js-batch-dom-css` - Group CSS changes via classes or cssText
111	- `js-index-maps` - Build Map for repeated lookups
112	- `js-cache-property-access` - Cache object properties in loops
113	- `js-cache-function-results` - Cache function results in module-level Map
114	- `js-cache-storage` - Cache localStorage/sessionStorage reads
115	- `js-combine-iterations` - Combine multiple filter/map into one loop
116	- `js-length-check-first` - Check array length before expensive comparison
117	- `js-early-exit` - Return early from functions
118	- `js-hoist-regexp` - Hoist RegExp creation outside loops
119	- `js-min-max-loop` - Use loop for min/max instead of sort
120	- `js-set-map-lookups` - Use Set/Map for O(1) lookups
121	- `js-tosorted-immutable` - Use toSorted() for immutability
122	- `js-flatmap-filter` - Use flatMap to map and filter in one pass
123	- `js-request-idle-callback` - Defer non-critical work to browser idle time
124	
125	### 8. Advanced Patterns (LOW)
126	
127	- `advanced-effect-event-deps` - Don't put `useEffectEvent` results in effect deps
128	- `advanced-event-handler-refs` - Store event handlers in refs
129	- `advanced-init-once` - Initialize app once per app load
130	- `advanced-use-latest` - useLatest for stable callback refs
